headline: ESCONDIDA SUPERVISORS WALK OUT — 1,020 WORKERS STRIKE AT WORLD'S LARGEST COPPER MINE
snippet: BHP's Escondida — the world's largest copper mine producing roughly 1.25 million tonnes annually — went on strike Wednesday after a 95% union vote and failed state mediation, with approximately 1,020 supervisors and staff walking off the job. This is a separate labour action from the Centinela strike already underway; supply disruption at Escondida is expected to intensify after approximately two weeks, compounding the existing Codelco and Centinela squeezes and adding material upside pressure to a copper price already approaching record highs.

headline: U.S. FIRMS EYE MALAYSIA RARE EARTHS — 12+ COMPANIES SCOUT AS CHINA'S NOV 10 DEADLINE APPROACHES
snippet: More than a dozen U.S. companies are evaluating mining projects and processing investments in Malaysia as Washington moves to cut dependence on China, after Beijing added MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to its export control blacklist in June, according to the U.S. Embassy in Kuala Lumpur. The push accelerates Southeast Asia's rare earth supply chain buildout just weeks before China's November 10 heavy rare earth export deadline, and follows the Malaysian king's personal acquisition of a stake in Southern Alliance Mining — which is expanding into rare earths in Johor — announced one day earlier.

headline: SSR MINING PAYS US$464M FOR ROXMORE'S CONVERSE GOLD — 5.2M NEVADA OUNCES, $200M IN SYNERGIES PROJECTED
snippet: SSR Mining (Nasdaq: SSRM) agreed October 13 to acquire Roxmore Resources at C$6.75 per share — a 27% premium — for a deal valued at US$464 million (or C$712 million total including a spinout vehicle funded with US$10 million), adding the Converse gold project's 2.2 million indicated and 3.0 million inferred ounces to a complex sitting 6 kilometres from its Marigold Mine on Nevada's Battle Mountain-Eureka Trend. SSR estimates at least $200 million in life-of-mine synergies, will fund the acquisition entirely from existing balance sheet cash, and expects closing in Q4 2026 — sending Roxmore shares 30.6% higher while SSR fell 7.3% on dilution concerns.

headline: GOLD SLIDES THIRD STRAIGHT SESSION TO $4,139 — DOLLAR AT 18-MONTH HIGH AHEAD OF CPI RELEASE
snippet: Spot gold fell for a third consecutive session Wednesday morning to $4,138.90 per ounce — down $21.20 on the day — with the U.S. dollar holding near an 18-month high and traders holding back ahead of the September CPI release, reversing optimism that had briefly lifted gold toward the $4,200 technical level earlier in the week. The pullback tests whether the $4,100–$4,165 range is establishing a floor ahead of the Federal Reserve's October 27–28 meeting, where traders are pricing a low but non-zero probability of a rate hike that has suppressed both bullion and junior mining valuations throughout October.

headline: SILVER FALLS BELOW $59, GOLD-SILVER RATIO HITS 71 — WHAT OCTOBER'S BREAKDOWN MEANS FOR JUNIOR MINERS
snippet: With spot silver at $58.56 — down from its January 2026 record of $121 per ounce — and the gold-silver ratio widening to approximately 71, Canadian Mining Report's October analysis examines whether Q4 holds a catalyst for silver's re-rating or an extended correction, citing the Silver Institute's projected sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces and the structural solar and electronics demand thesis against ongoing rate headwinds. The analysis flags $62 and $70 as key threshold levels for junior silver developers: a sustained break above $70 has historically triggered sector re-ratings, while a close below $62 would signal further equity compression for TSX-V and ASX silver explorers heading into year-end.

headline: LYNAS TO BUILD BRAZIL RARE EARTH SEPARATION PLANT — BNDES WEIGHS BILLIONS AS METEORIC DEAL ADVANCES
snippet: Lynas Rare Earths (ASX: LYC) has unveiled plans for a rare earth oxide separation plant in Brazil's Minas Gerais state — tied to its A$968 million all-scrip acquisition of Meteoric Resources, whose Caldeira project has a completed DFS and a Preliminary Environmental Licence already granted — with state development bank BNDES evaluating potential financing and Brazil's Mines and Energy Minister publicly confirming the government is considering backing it. If built, the facility would become one of the largest rare earth processing plants outside China at a strategically critical moment — weeks before China's November 10 heavy rare earth export restrictions take effect and as the U.S. scrambles to diversify its rare earth supply chain.

headline: COPPER EYES RECORD $6.80/LB AS BULLISH ECONOMIC DATA MEETS THREE-MINE SUPPLY SQUEEZE IN CHILE
snippet: LME copper climbed toward $6.80 per pound Wednesday — within reach of its September record high — as improving economic indicators in the U.S. and China reinforced the demand thesis just as the Escondida supervisor walkout compounded existing supply disruptions at Centinela and Codelco's El Teniente on Chile's copper corridor. Junior copper explorers in Canada and Australia have historically seen material equity re-ratings when copper spot price sustains new record highs for more than one session, making this week's convergence of demand strength and simultaneous multi-mine supply disruption one of the strongest copper setups in the current bull cycle.

headline: FATHOM NICKEL FILES MAIDEN 3.1M-TONNE Ni-Cu-Co RESOURCE AT GOCHAGER LAKE — DEPOSIT OPEN AT DEPTH
snippet: Fathom Nickel (CSE: FNI) filed its NI 43-101 technical report October 13 for the maiden resource at Gochager Lake in Saskatchewan's Rottenstone Domain, confirming 858,701 indicated tonnes at 0.57% nickel equivalent and 3.1 million inferred tonnes at 0.45% NiEq — a system open along its 300-metre strike and to 450 metres depth that was delineated from just 17 drill holes. The Ni-Cu-Co deposit joins a growing pipeline of Canadian nickel-battery metal discoveries gaining strategic relevance as North American EV manufacturers seek non-Chinese critical mineral supply chains, and September 2026 drill results already identified new zones of semi-massive to massive sulphide mineralization outside the maiden resource boundary.

headline: NORD PRECIOUS METALS CONFIRMS 2.81M OZ SILVER AT ONTARIO TAILINGS — NI 43-101 FILED, REPROCESSING NEXT
snippet: Nord Precious Metals (TSXV: NTH) filed its NI 43-101 technical report October 13 for the Gowganda Silver Tailings Project in Ontario, confirming an Indicated Mineral Resource of 1.845 million tonnes at 47.4 grams per tonne silver for 2.814 million contained ounces — a fully surface-accessible deposit in an established Ontario mining jurisdiction that requires no underground development. With the Northern Miner noting the silver price surge earlier in 2026 has 'revived' the project and metallurgical testwork now underway, Nord is advancing toward process selection, engineering design, and environmental permitting for what could be a low-capex silver producer at a time when the sector is searching for near-term development assets.

headline: URANIUM FUEL CYCLE STOCKS OUTPERFORM AS BURKE HOLLOW GOES LIVE AND KAZATOMPROM DELAYS DEEPEN
snippet: A Motley Fool analysis published October 13 argues that uranium fuel cycle companies — conversion, enrichment, and fuel fabrication — are the overlooked plays in the nuclear renaissance, with spot U₃O₈ holding near $90 per pound and long-term contracts above $96.50 per pound while the Kazatomprom TQZ sulfuric acid plant delays (now pushed to 2027–2028) continue to tighten 2027 supply models. The piece cites Uranium Energy Corp's Burke Hollow startup in South Texas as the first new U.S. ISR operation in over a decade and Global Atomic's $414 million U.S. DFC loan conditional approval for the Dasa mine in Niger as evidence that Western governments are moving aggressively to rebuild uranium supply chains before the next reactor generation comes online.
